This GitHub release is a prerelease because its public surfaces are classified as alpha or experimental. The WebAssembly source is version `0.3.0`, but the observed npm package remains at `0.2.0` because it was not published with this release. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#surface-summary))

## Who should upgrade?

- Upgrade from Rust `0.2.x` if you need the new text-line, per-axis table, CJK, right-to-left, rotation, tagged-PDF, or malformed-content handling and can accept an alpha API. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#rust))
- Evaluate the Python `pdfplumber-rs` package if you are migrating a scoped Python `pdfplumber` v0.11.10 workflow, can validate it against the published compatibility gaps, and will use an isolated environment. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- Upgrade the source-built Command-Line Interface if its expanded extraction commands are useful and you do not require prebuilt binaries or stable structured-output schemas. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#command-line-interface))
- Do not adopt this release as a complete Python drop-in replacement, a cross-browser or production-ready WebAssembly release, or evidence of a cross-project performance advantage. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#features-and-known-limitations))

## Behavior changes

The [v0.3.0 changelog entry](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#030---2026-08-22) is the canonical change record.

### Added

- **API:** Added the Python `pdfplumber` facade with `open`, lazy `PDF.pages`, page
  selection and geometry, crop relationships, cache flushing, object dictionaries,
  annotations, hyperlinks, structure trees, and JSON/CSV serialization. The Python
  extension remains alpha and is not yet a complete drop-in replacement. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/readiness/v0.3.0.md#ready-workflows))
- **Platform:** Versioned the Rust crate, Python distribution, CLI crate, and
  WebAssembly source at `0.3.0` under Apache-2.0. Rust, Python, and CLI are alpha;
  WebAssembly is experimental, and its npm package was not published with this
  release and therefore remained at `0.2.0`. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#surface-summary))

### Changed

- **Performance:** Changed word-to-line clustering to use y-coordinate buckets so it
  avoids repeatedly comparing words from unrelated rows. No cross-project performance
  result is claimed by this release. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/crates/pdfplumber/benches/README.md#benchmark-suite))
- **Migration:** Breaking: `UnicodeNorm::default()` changed from no normalization to
  NFC. Select `UnicodeNorm::None` explicitly when byte-for-byte preservation of
  decomposed text is required. The Rust `MarkdownOptions`, `MarkdownRenderer`, and
  `Page::to_markdown` APIs, plus CLI Markdown output, were removed; render Markdown in
  a downstream integration instead. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))

### Fixed

- **Compatibility:** Expanded text, word, table, page-geometry, font, CJK, RTL,
  rotation, tagged-PDF, and malformed-content handling against Python
  `pdfplumber`. The Python compatibility target is pinned to v0.11.10 and remains
  evidence-scoped rather than a blanket parity claim. ([evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/readiness/v0.3.0.md#ready-workflows))

## Known limitations

- **Rust:** The 0.3.x API is alpha and may change before the stable contract is complete. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#rust))
- **Rust:** Required CI verifies Ubuntu Linux only; registry installation and other targets are not smoke-tested. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#rust))
- **Rust:** The current-source Rust quick start passes, but published 0.3.0 predates Pdf::open_path and its recorded cold registry trial fails compilation. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#rust))
- **Rust:** Image-only PDFs require a separate Optical Character Recognition stage. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#rust))
- **Python:** Compatibility is incomplete and is not yet a full drop-in replacement. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** The current-source policy for the next Python release supports exactly CPython 3.13 on Ubuntu for both the wheel and source distribution. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** Published Python 0.3.0 metadata predates the current-source policy and still advertises Python 3.9 and PyPy; those immutable legacy classifiers are not support evidence. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** Python 3.14 and PyPy are explicitly unsupported by the next-release source metadata and are not release targets. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** Linux auditwheel inspection proves artifact compatibility metadata and non-policy shared-library independence; it is not installation or runtime evidence for a Linux distribution. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** macOS installed-wheel execution is on macOS 15; matching Mach-O 10.12 and 11.0 deployment metadata is not runtime evidence from those minimum operating-system releases. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** Windows installed-wheel execution is on Windows Server 2025 x86-64 with LongPathsEnabled=1; it is not evidence for disabled long-path policy, other Windows versions or architectures, or every filesystem configuration. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Python:** Co-installation with the Python `pdfplumber` distribution is unsupported; use a fresh environment containing exactly one distribution. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#python))
- **Command-Line Interface:** The Rust-native subcommand interface does not yet match Python pdfplumber's positional Command-Line Interface contract. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#command-line-interface))
- **Command-Line Interface:** Native archive smoke coverage is limited to one deterministic text-to-JSON fixture; it does not prove every subcommand or PDF class. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#command-line-interface))
- **Command-Line Interface:** Stable structured-output schemas and exit codes remain open work. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#command-line-interface))
- **Command-Line Interface:** Attestations bind the GitHub workflow identity and exact bytes; they do not prove security, reproducibility, broader compatibility, or post-publication registry installation. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#command-line-interface))
- **WebAssembly:** The surface is experimental; the prepublication gate covers one maintained Chromium build and does not establish compatibility with every browser. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#webassembly))
- **WebAssembly:** The observed npm release is 0.2.0 while the repository source is 0.3.0. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#webassembly))
- **WebAssembly:** Bundle size, startup time, memory, cross-browser behavior, and published-registry installation are independent gates. ([support evidence](https://github.com/developer0hye/pdfplumber-rs/blob/main/docs/support.md#webassembly))
